title: November 18 — WaveFormer: resonant recurrence with attention
summary: WaveFormer V1 trained on three RTX 3060 seeds: all models reached 100% on 24-token role retrieval. Wave scored 83.0% at 48 versus 77.0% attention and 78.5% leaky, but zeroing the recurrent head changed mean accuracy negligibly; the retained attention pathway appears sufficient. V2 now introduces a locality cutoff forcing long-range recall through recurrence. Full V2 results pending.

nodes.claim: Tiny two-block WaveFormer V1 tests attention against leaky and phase-rotating recurrent head on paired synthetic role memory; V2 isolates recurrence with a short local-attention window and out-of-reach writes.
nodes.survived: V1 800-step runs (seeds 42–44) confirm all arms learn 24-token training task at 100%; 48-token held-out averages: attention 76.95%, leaky 78.45%, wave 83.01%. V2 source and unit tests implement an explicit memory cutoff: local attention receptive field reaches 6 prior positions, target writes at least 9 back.
nodes.killed: V1 accuracy ablation gives no evidence that the recurrent head carries answers: wave 48-token accuracy 83.01% intact and 83.14% with its recurrent head removed; at 96 tokens attention wins 56.12% to wave 54.62%. Training wall time is longer for wave (~56 s/seed) than attention (~14 s), though kernels are unoptimized. V2 full trained results pending; no wave-specific memory or efficiency advantage yet.

edges.why: Off-token concept transfer motivates a learned recurrent read/write interface, but there is no shared implementation.
The two-form content/prediction distinction informs a proposed resonant head; waves have not yet earned a numerical advantage.
Distributed persistent context motivates future local gates, not yet implemented in WaveFormer.

motifs.title: Precise attention alongside persistent recurrent state
motifs.description: Proposed learned resonant recurrence compared with ordinary attention and a nonoscillatory recurrent control; no outcome yet.
